newsitem.title: USA: California Pro in talks to boost value.
newsitem.headline: California Pro in talks to boost value.

text.p: California Pro Sports Inc, reporting a loss for the third quarter, said it is talking with an investment banking group about its alternatives in an effort to boost shareholder value.
The company said it is beginning to revamp its product line and is in discussions with its majority-owned USA Skate to design and market in-line skates and snowboards.
California Pro owns 57 percent of USA Skate, according to Chief Financial Officer Barry Hollander.
The product revamp will be overseen by Jon Hodgins, former executive vice president of CCM/Sport Maska Inc, California Pro said.

"Management is confident this arrangement will enhance the overall sales performance of the company and will allow for an estimated reduction of nearly $2 million of selling, general, and administrative costs currently incurred by California Pro," the company said in the third-quarter earnings release.
"The company is confident that these actions will assist in the restoration of profitability," it said.
The third quarter resulted in a net loss of $631,184, or $0.15 per share, compared with profit of $63,942, or $0.02 per share, for the quarter ended September 30, 1995.
California Pro's revenues for the period were $6,230,078 compared with $3,783,828.

The company said third-quarter results were hurt by a non-cash charge of $394,872 of market to market revaluation of securities. Also affecting the period was $187,000 of interest on notes payable from the acquisition of USA Skate, and $186,471 of additional depreciation and amortization absorbed as a result of the USA Skate transaction.
The company said also that its operations were affected by the soft retail market conditions for in-line skates and snowboards.
